title: Chapter 65 — Penetration: One Project to All Projects
intro: The penetration ladder and the share-growth playbook per buyer type.

sections.title: Penetration Feels Like Service
sections.content:
Penetration feels like service because the flow already exists — you are consolidating friction, not creating demand. The builder is already doing projects. They are already buying appliances. You are making it easier for them to buy everything from one source.

'You have been using us for cooking. What about the laundry on your next project? I can add it to the same delivery run and save your team a coordination step.'

sections.title: The Penetration Ladder
sections.content:
Level 1: They use you for one category on one project. Level 2: They use you for all categories on selected projects. Level 3: They use you for all categories on all projects. Level 4: They refer you to other builders.

Each level requires earning trust at the current level before asking for the next. Do not jump from Level 1 to Level 3 — that is asking for too much too fast. Prove yourself on one category. Then expand to the next.

sections.title: Category Expansion Tactics
sections.content:
After a successful cooking package delivery, say: 'That went smoothly. For your next project, want me to add laundry to the spec? I can bundle it into the same delivery and give you package pricing.'

After every successful delivery, plant the seed for the next category. The expansion is gradual, natural, and built on proven performance.
